aliases: A user account was locked out
analysis: Prioritize lockouts involving privileged, service, break-glass or otherwise high-value accounts, especially when the caller computer is unexpected.
Use Caller Computer Name as an origin pivot but do not treat it as a guaranteed source identity; the field can be blank, stale or insufficient by itself.
Correlate the minutes preceding 4740 with 4625, 4771 and 4776 to distinguish password guessing from a single stale-credential source repeatedly retrying authentication.
If the Subject Security ID is not the expected SYSTEM context, inspect the account-management path more closely because the lockout was not emitted under the common system context.

collection.interpretation_note: Event 4740 records the lockout outcome, not the complete cause. Repeated bad passwords, stale stored credentials, services, scheduled tasks, mapped resources, mobile/VPN clients or hostile password guessing can all precede the same lockout. Correlate earlier authentication failures before attributing intent.
requirements: Audit User Account Management success auditing must be enabled where account-lockout telemetry is required.
Collection should preserve preceding authentication failures and endpoint/service context so the lockout can be traced back to its credential source.
collection.scope_note: Microsoft documents this event for user-account lockouts on domain controllers, member servers and workstations. Caller Computer Name is operationally useful but can be blank or incomplete and is a computer name rather than an IP address.

correlations.purpose: identify failed logon attempts immediately preceding the lockout and extract logon type, process and network context
identify Kerberos pre-authentication failures that accumulated before the lockout
identify NTLM credential validation failures associated with the same lockout sequence
determine whether a successful logon occurred before or after the lockout window
trace stale credentials to services, scheduled tasks, scripts, mapped resources, VPN clients or stored credentials on the originating endpoint

The certificate issuer, serial-number and thumbprint fields are schema-visible but documented by Microsoft as empty for Event 4771.

failure_code.meaning: KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN — client principal was not found in the Kerberos database.
KDC_ERR_POLICY — the KDC rejected the request because of policy.
KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP — the KDC does not support the requested encryption type.
KDC_ERR_PADATA_TYPE_NOSUPP — the KDC does not support the requested pre-authentication data type.
KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED — the client credentials are revoked or otherwise not currently usable.
KDC_ERR_KEY_EXPIRED — the account password/key has expired.
KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED — pre-authentication information was invalid; commonly caused by an incorrect password.
KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW — client and KDC clocks differ beyond the accepted Kerberos skew.
KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED — integrity validation indicates the message stream was modified or could not be validated.
